correctness.rationale: Let \(q\) be the exponent of the finite commutator subgroup. In a class-two group, \([x^q,y]=[x,y]^q\), hence \(U_i=T_i^q\) commute. For every residue \(r\) modulo \(q\), \(P_{i,r}(m)=(p_i(qm+r)-p_i(r))/q\) lies in \(\mathbb Z[m]\) and preserves polynomial independence. Each \(U_i\) is totally ergodic, so the published commuting independent-polynomial theorem gives the product limit on that residue class; finite recombination gives the full \(L^2\) limit. No finite experiment is used as a proof.

value.rationale: The finite commutator condition is a natural structural boundary inside the source's open 2-step nilpotent problem. The result resolves all independent polynomial shapes on this entire boundary and shows that a genuinely noncommutative obstruction to the conjecture must involve infinite commutator directions. This is a motivated structural reduction, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
